text_blocks.snippet: Yes, the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) does drug test employees, particularly for pre-employment and in certain situations after hire. UAB is committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace.

list.snippet: UAB requires pre-employment drug screens for many positions, including those in UAB Medicine, UAB Police Department, Facilities, Animal Resource Program, and some temporary service roles.
Candidates must sign a consent form agreeing to the drug test before it can be administered.
Refusal to sign the consent form will disqualify the candidate.
UAB may also conduct drug testing for reasonable cause, as outlined in HR Policy 634.
This policy also covers reporting and reviewing drug test results.
UAB may also conduct drug testing as required by federal, state, or industry regulations.
UAB Medicine requires new employees to undergo a pre-employment physical and drug screen, as well as TB screenings and respirator FIT testing (if applicable).
UAB Medicine also requires annual flu shots.
Some positions may require additional screenings like basic or advanced life support certifications.
UAB's commitment to a drug-free work and educational environment is outlined in the UAB Drug-Free Campus and Workplace Policy.
This policy applies to all members of the UAB community, including students, faculty, and staff.
Employees who abuse alcohol or drugs are considered a danger to themselves, coworkers, patients, and students.
UAB also has an impaired program to address substance abuse issues, Human Resources policy.
